subject: determine file extension specified by user for file download

messages.author: 66aaf5d139ba9c7f
messages.subject: determine file extension specified by user for file download
parts:
The first function below seems to work. However, I would like to get the 2nd function to work so a users can choose filetype based on the file extension chosen. I thought I would be able to access the extension provided by the user through file or filename. That doesn't seem to work however.

output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
filename = function() { paste(input$datasets[1], '.rda', sep='') },
  content = function(file) {

  ext <- tolower(file_ext(file))
  robj <- input$datasets[1]
  assign(robj, getdata())
  save(list = robj, file = file)
  }
)

output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
filename = function() { paste(input$datasets[1], '.rda', sep='') },
  content = function(file) {

 ext <- tolower(file_ext(file))
 robj <- input$datasets[1]
 assign(robj, getdata())

if(ext == 'rda' || ext == 'rdata') {
   save(list = robj, file = file)
} 
else if(ext == 'dta') {
write.dta(get(robj), file)
} else if(ext == 'csv') {
write.csv(get(robj), file)
} else {
cat("Selected data-type not (yet) supported.\n Use .rda, .csv, or .dta\n")
}
  }
)

messages.subject: Re: determine file extension specified by user for file download
parts:
I found a work-around:

In ui.R I have:

selectInput("saveAs", "", choices = c('rda','csv','dta'), selected = NULL, multiple = FALSE),
downloadButton('downloadData', 'Save data'),
tags$style(type='text/css', "#downloadData { vertical-align: top;}"),

In server.R

output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
  filename = function() { paste(input$datasets[1],'.',input$saveAs, sep='') },
  content = function(file) {

ext <- input$saveAs

robj <- input$datasets[1]
assign(robj, getdata())

if(ext == 'rda' || ext == 'rdata') {
                save(list = robj, file = file)
} 
else if(ext == 'dta') {
write.dta(get(robj), file)
} else if(ext == 'csv') {
write.csv(get(robj), file)
}
   }

)

See https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radyant for an example
